note: Human-curated, verified mapping from raw LLM-extracted predicate text to a governed predicate_id in GMV_ONTOLOGY_REGISTRY_v0.1.json. Populated from real rejection-queue data (Task 7) observed on a real biography extraction (Federico Garibaldi, this session) -- NOT an exhaustive vocabulary, NOT LLM-guessed. Every entry here was checked by a human against the target predicate's real domain/range before being added; this is exactly the 'verified fact, not inference' principle already applied to area35_known_artists.json.
note_on_scope: Deliberately tiny. Several other real raw predicates seen in the same document ('acquired', 'was born in', 'earned', 'presented', 'is an', 'explores') do NOT appear here: 'acquired' would need the inverse direction of owned_by (subject/object swapped), which this mapping does not attempt; the rest have no corresponding predicate in the registry at all today -- a real vocabulary gap, not a missing mapping.
note_on_maintenance: Adding an entry here is a governance decision (reuse-before-invention, same rule GMV_ONTOLOGY_REGISTRY_v0.1.json states for predicates themselves) -- not something code should do automatically from the rejection queue's frequency counts. A human reads the queue, decides, then edits this file.
note_on_task36_exclusions: Task 36 (2026-10-05) examined SEVEN high-frequency exhibition-participation candidates from the rejection queue against real source documents and mapped exactly ONE of them ('held at', above). The other six are DELIBERATELY NOT mapped, each for a concrete reason verified against real extractions -- recorded here so that a future reader who sees their counts in the queue does not add them back on frequency or name-similarity alone, which is the exact failure mode this project has already shipped twice. 'held': split across two real documents of the SAME biography into incompatible shapes -- the 80 cases in 'Bio completa EN - Ernesto Morales.pdf.md' have subject=Ernesto Morales (a PERSON) and object=show title (participated_in-shaped), while the 52 cases in 'Bio completa EN - IT Ernesto Morales.doc.md' have subject=exhibition title ('Al Infinito', 'Astrolabio da viaggio', ...) and object=venue (located_at-shaped); the pipeline cannot tell which is which from the text alone, and 0/132 of those objects link to an entity from the same extraction, so it would build 0 atoms regardless. 'present': split -- 36 of 210 real cases are OCR garbage with subject_raw == object_raw, i.e. not a relation at all. 'exhibited': split -- the object is sometimes an exhibition title and sometimes a gallery, and INSTITUTION is outside participated_in's range [EVENT,EXHIBITION,PROJECT]. 'exhibited at': split -- 49 real cases are located_at-shaped (exhibition -> venue) but all 7 real cases in cv_davide_genna.docx have a PERSON as subject, which is exactly the Task 22 Garibaldi located_at mis-application; located_at's domain does not include PERSON and no mechanical check enforces the domain. 'mostra': not one shape -- real subjects are variously the literal word 'Mostra', a venue, and a show title. 'presente': not a relation at all in its only real source -- object_raw is the word 'presente' itself, used as a caption. Re-adding any of these requires a fresh real-document domain/range review, not a re-count.

mappings.verified_against: located_at domain=[EXHIBITION,EVENT,ORGANIZATION] range=[PLACE] -- checked against real Garibaldi cases: 'AttraversaMenti was held at Le Stanze della Fotografia' (subject is an exhibition), 'Through, Let's Hope Time Won't Be Late was held at Area35 Art Gallery' (same shape).
Same predicate/range as 'was held at' -- checked against 'BlueShores was presented at UniCredit Pavilion, Milan', same subject/object shape (a titled show/work presented at a venue).

Confirmed on TWO separate re-extractions of the same real Garibaldi biography (gemma4:12b is not deterministic between runs): both times produced 'AttraversaMenti' | 'was a solo exhibition at' | 'Le Stanze della Fotografia, Venice (2025)' -- exact same subject/object shape already verified for 'was held at' above, a stable paraphrase, not a new semantic case.

Corrected 2026-09-21 (was wrongly mapped to exhibited_at, which has domain=[ARTWORK_INSTANCE] -- the subject must be a specific artwork, not a person; caught on review, not caught by the confirming session itself). participated_in has domain=[PERSON,ARTIST] range=[EVENT,EXHIBITION,PROJECT], which matches the real case exactly: 'Giovanni Cerri' (subject=ARTIST) | 'ha esposto' | '54° Biennale di Venezia, Padiglione Italia' (object=EXHIBITION), from 'Nel 2011 l’artista ha esposto alla 54° Biennale di Venezia, Padiglione Italia, a cura di Vittorio Sgarbi.'

located_at domain=[EXHIBITION,EVENT,ORGANIZATION] range=[PLACE,INSTITUTION] -- checked against 76 distinct real 'held at' cases from one real source document (01_artists/morales_ernesto/10_md_processed_files/07_career__01_biography__bio completa en - ernesto morales.doc.md), re-extracted for this entry rather than trusted from the rejection queue. 63 distinct subjects, EVERY one an exhibition/show/fair title and ZERO person subjects (checked explicitly against that document's own extracted entity list, not inferred from the word 'held'); 67 distinct objects, all real venues (galleries, cultural centres, embassies, museums, civic buildings, cities). Same subject/object shape already verified above for 'was held at'/'was presented at'/'presente in' -- including a venue cited for both: 'Le città dell'esilio' | 'held at' | 'Galleria Il Sole Arte Contemporanea' (that same gallery is already the 'presente in' citation above); 'Equinox –' | 'held at' | 'William Holman Art Gallery'; 'Identidades' | 'held at' | 'Centro Cultural Recoleta'; 'En el sueño de Polifilo' | 'held at' | 'Galleria Raffaella De Chirico Arte Contemporanea'. COUNTER-SHAPE CHECKED AND FOUND ABSENT: a bare 'held at' whose subject is a PERSON does not occur in this corpus (0/76). KNOWN LIMITATION, deliberately not solved here: validate_atom() checks only object_type against the predicate's range and never checks the subject against the domain (verified: gmv_atom_validator.py has no reference to 'domain' at all), so this entry's correctness rests on the human domain review above, exactly like the pre-existing 'was held at'/'presente in' entries -- a future 'held at' sentence whose subject is a person and whose object is a real linked venue would build an atom no mechanical check would catch. SCOPE OF THE EVIDENCE, stated honestly: all 76 cases come from ONE real source document; the two other real variants of the same biography ('...EN - Ernesto Morales.pdf.md' and '...EN - IT Ernesto Morales.doc.md') emit the bare text 'held' for these very same facts instead of 'held at', which is why 'held' is excluded below rather than treated as a synonym of this entry.
